flagship_directive: Construct an observable confidence procedure over the same all-C model class and prove a matching uniformly honest expected-length frontier, including the q_C asymptotic boundary layer.
critique: The proved result is a matched cardinality-uniform MSE frontier over the stated binary-action finite-state union, including the unit-overlap boundary and shrinking-radius regimes; the framing does not depend on an open conjecture or overstate the theorem. Its reach is limited by the strong, latent, empirically untestable stationary-overlap restriction and the requirement that both policy-induced kernels satisfy uniform contraction. The converse allows latent cardinality to grow as O(log T), so it does not establish the same phenomenon for a physically fixed hidden-state model, while the application supplies only a custom 360-state bias witness with a loose C=720 certificate rather than evidence for the original simulator or finite-sample risk performance. These scope and validation limits keep the completed package below flagship.
